title: Saxclaviats
identity: The 2010 Saxophone Catalogue lists Lepage’s Saxclaviats for E-flat or B-flat saxophone and piano. A Luxembourg government examination repertoire list places it in a lower-division first-mention list and also specifies E-flat or B-flat. The current catalog’s soprano designation is not supported by these records.

evidence.claim: The catalogue PDF directly lists Lepage, Saxclaviats, for E-flat or B-flat saxophone and piano; it does not identify soprano specifically.
evidence.source_name: Johan van der Linden, Saxophone Catalogue 2010

evidence.claim: The Luxembourg Commission nationale des programmes de l’enseignement musical lists Saxclaviats for E-flat and B-flat saxophone in the “répertoire-type pour l’examen de fin de cycle” under the lower-division first-mention section. This is a documented examination context, not a college placement.
evidence.source_name: Luxembourg Ministry of Education, Saxophone study program

evidence.claim: The opened 2010 Saxophone Catalogue lists E-flat or B-flat saxophone and piano.
evidence.source_name: Johan van der Linden, Saxophone Catalogue 2010

review_focus: The publisher edition and actual parts should be checked to determine whether the catalog’s soprano entry corresponds to a separate version.
collection_flag: The Luxembourg ministry documents a lower-division examination-list use. This is documented school/conservatory context, not a college placement or level recommendation.

score_links.description: Opened Luxembourg government saxophone program; lists the work and instrument options but contains no score notation.

gaps: No accessible notation for the Combre edition was located after checking publisher and score-preview leads.
The sources list E-flat and B-flat options, but no soprano-specific edition has been verified.
No saxophone recording or college/professional use verified.
